findings.description: The loop at line 1112 iterates j <= keys_result->numkeys, but slot_buffer is allocated for numkeys ints (line 1110) and keys_result->keys has only numkeys valid entries (0..numkeys-1). The final iteration reads keys[numkeys].pos -- a zero-filled keysbuf entry (pos 0, hashing argv[0]) for <=6 keys and a heap out-of-bounds read for >6 keys -- and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] past the heap allocation at line 1115. The base version used j < numkeys; the fix is to restore j < numkeys (the dead slot_buffer can be removed entirely).
findings.failureMode: Any keyed command in cluster mode triggers a heap buffer overflow and out-of-bounds read, causing memory corruption or a crash, and single-key commands are spuriously reported as CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT when the command name hashes to a different slot.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop in extractSlotFromKeysResult reads and writes out of bounds

findings.description: The new code calls malloc at line 1110 and free at lines 1120 and 1124, violating the repository mandate to use the zmalloc/zfree wrappers; src/server.h marks malloc/free deprecated for exactly this reason. Running make -C src cluster.o with REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror" fails with three deprecated-declaration errors at these lines, and the allocation bypasses Redis memory accounting with an unchecked return value. Replace malloc/free with zmalloc/zfree, or remove the unused slot_buffer allocation.
findings.failureMode: The mandated -Werror build fails to compile, and at runtime the allocation is untracked by Redis memory accounting and dereferenced without a NULL check on allocation failure.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free instead of zmalloc/zfree in extractSlotFromKeysResult

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction in BrowserViewControllerState now returns displayView .readerModeLongPressAction instead of base .readerMode. In BrowserViewController, .readerMode calls toggleReaderMode() while .readerModeLongPressAction calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which creates a reading-list record; a separate handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction already maps the long-press action to that display type. Fix: restore displayView .readerMode in handleShowReaderModeAction.
findings.failureMode: Tapping the Reader Mode toolbar button adds the page to the reading list instead of entering or exiting Reader Mode.
findings.title: Reader Mode tap now triggers reading-list long-press action

findings.description: Base code kept the URL only when currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL; the diff changes this to isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL. Reader Mode URLs are http://localhost/reader-mode/page URLs (URLExtension.isReaderModeURL) and therefore also satisfy isWebPage(), so the change reverses the exclusion; AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction then uses toolbarAction.url in preference to state.url. Fix: restore (currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL).
findings.failureMode: Cancelling edit mode on a Reader Mode page restores the internal localhost Reader Mode URL in the address bar instead of preserving the page URL state.
findings.title: cancelEditMode now passes Reader Mode internal URLs

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry maps .available to false and all other states to true, inverting the base true/false mapping. The retained comment says .available means Reader Mode will be enabled after the action executes, so .available must record isEnabled true when passed to readerModeButtonTapped. Fix: restore case .available: true and default: false.
findings.failureMode: Every Reader Mode button tap records the opposite enabled state in telemetry, corrupting Reader Mode enable/disable metrics.
findings.title: Reader Mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description: The diff changes private let gleanWrapper to internal let gleanWrapper with no external caller: grep found no access to a ToolbarTelemetry instance's gleanWrapper outside its own initializer. AGENTS.md rule 11 requires implementation details to stay private with minimal exposure. Fix: restore private let gleanWrapper.
findings.failureMode: Module-internal code can access and record through gleanWrapper directly, bypassing ToolbarTelemetry's API and violating the access-control mandate.
findings.title: ToolbarTelemetry gleanWrapper access widened from private

findings.description: CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer.render_template does result.get("result") and the guard `rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` lets None through to `return rendered` at line 40, violating the declared -> str. Running basedpyright and mypy on the changed production files both report incompatible return type str | None vs str at this line. Fix the renderer to raise TemplateRenderError when rendered is not a str, including None.
findings.failureMode: Type-check CI fails, and TemplateTransformNode._run calls len(None) raising TypeError instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult when the executor result is missing or None.
findings.title: Renderer can return None despite str return type

findings.description: Newly added tests starting at line 455 (repeated at lines 488, 519, 549 and through 1144) pass graph=mock_graph and a flat config=node_data dict. The added TemplateTransformNode.__init__ and Node.__init__ accept no graph argument and require config containing id and data; a probe reproduced TypeError for graph and ValueError Node ID is required for the flat config, while a correct {id, data} config succeeds. Fix the tests to drop graph and wrap node data under data; the implementation contract is correct per Node and the integration test.
findings.failureMode: Every newly added test fails with TypeError before reaching _run when the spec file is run explicitly, so the added renderer coverage never executes.
findings.title: New tests construct TemplateTransformNode with unsupported graph argument and flat config

findings.description: The newly added assert at line 1031 uses a Yoda condition `"1, two, 3.0, True" == result.outputs["output"]`. Running ruff check on the changed files reproduced a SIM300 error at this line, violating mandate 2 requiring Ruff to pass. Fix by swapping the operands to result.outputs["output"] == "1, two, 3.0, True".
findings.failureMode: ruff check (make check) fails with SIM300 on this line.
findings.title: Yoda condition violates Ruff SIM300

findings.description: Line 309 changes write_and_make_executable to return Result<(), FileWriteError>, and prepare_tools (returning crate::Result) propagates it with `?` at lines 232, 239, 245, 251 and 259, but crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs has no From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error (only From<io::Error> and other listed types). The manual Display/Error impls at lines 291-307 also violate AGENTS.md rule 8 requiring thiserror for custom error enums, and the added chain makes line 312 fail rustfmt. Fix by restoring std::io::Result<()> (or deriving thiserror and adding a #[from] variant to crate::Error).
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler does not compile because the `?` operator cannot convert FileWriteError into crate::Error.
findings.title: FileWriteError has no conversion to crate::Error and breaks build

findings.description: Line 243 changed the base `if !gtk.exists()` guard to `if gtk.exists()`, while the parallel gstreamer block at line 249 correctly keeps `!gstreamer.exists()`. On a fresh tools cache the inlined linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is therefore never written, so the unconditional `--plugin gtk` linuxdeploy invocation cannot find it. Fix by restoring `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: First-time AppImage bundling fails because linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is missing from the tools directory.
findings.title: Inverted gtk exists check skips plugin on fresh cache

findings.description: The base write_and_make_executable wrote the file first and then set mode 0o770; lines 312-313 swap the order to call fs::set_permissions before fs::write. All callers invoke it only when the destination does not yet exist (for example lines 228, 237 and 249), so set_permissions fails with NotFound and the data is never written. Fix by writing the file before setting permissions.
findings.failureMode: On a fresh cache every prepare_tools download/inline write fails with a permissions NotFound error, aborting AppImage bundling.
findings.title: set_permissions called before file is written

findings.description: Line 235 maps `i686` to `linuxdeploy_arch` and line 236 uses it for the local filename, but line 238 changed the download URL from `linuxdeploy-{linuxdeploy_arch}.AppImage` in the base to `linuxdeploy-{arch}.AppImage`. For arch `i686` the URL no longer matches the mapped artifact name the code intends to fetch. Fix by using `{linuxdeploy_arch}` in the download URL.
findings.failureMode: Bundling for i686 fails with a failed or wrong linuxdeploy download (404) on a fresh cache.
findings.title: linuxdeploy URL uses arch instead of linuxdeploy_arch

findings.description: The loop uses j <= keys_result->numkeys where the base used j < numkeys, so the final iteration reads keys_result->keys[numkeys].pos and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] into an allocation of only numkeys ints. For a single-key command the zero-initialized keysbuf gives pos 0, hashing argv[0] (the command name) as a phantom key and usually returning a false CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT; for more than MAX_KEYS_BUFFER keys, getKeysPrepareResult allocates keys at exactly numkeys entries, so the read is a heap out-of-bounds read whose garbage pos is dereferenced via argv[pos]. The slot_buffer write is a heap out-of-bounds write on every same-slot command that reaches it.
findings.failureMode: Cluster-mode keyed commands are falsely rejected as cross-slot, corrupt the heap, or crash the server; change the loop bound to j < keys_result->numkeys.
findings.title: Off-by-one in extractSlotFromKeysResult reads and writes past buffers

findings.description: The new code calls malloc at line 1110 and free at lines 1120 and 1124, violating AGENTS.md rule 2 requiring zmalloc/zfree, and src/server.h marks malloc/free deprecated. Running make -C src cluster.o with REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror" fails with three deprecated-declaration errors at exactly those lines, while the other changed objects compile cleanly. The allocation also bypasses zmalloc used-memory accounting and its return value is never checked before slot_buffer[j] is written.
findings.failureMode: The mandated -Werror build fails on cluster.o; remove the dead slot_buffer allocation or replace malloc/free with zmalloc/zfree.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free violates zmalloc mandate and fails the -Werror build

findings.description: The guard at line 38 (`if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)`) exempts None, so `return rendered` at line 40 returns None despite the declared `-> str` return type. Full basedpyright (`make type-check`) fails with exactly this error: template_renderer.py:40:16 "Type str | None is not assignable to return type str". A probe with an executor returning {"result": None} or {} confirms render_template returns None, after which TemplateTransformNode._run crashes on len(rendered) instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult; the fix is to raise TemplateRenderError whenever the result is not a str, including None.
findings.failureMode: A code executor response with a missing or None "result" makes the node raise TypeError from len(None) instead of a handled FAILED result, and the basedpyright type-check gate fails on this line.
findings.title: Renderer returns None for missing/None result instead of raising TemplateRenderError

findings.description: This field always binds the status select to trigger.expect, while FlowRunStateTriggerFields (lines 21-25) and the new DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (line 31) bind Proactive ("Stays in") selections to trigger.after and Reactive selections to trigger.expect. Selecting Stays in + Paused therefore submits expect=["prefect.work-pool.paused"], a proactive absence-of-paused trigger, instead of after=["prefect.work-pool.paused"]. The fix is to select the field name from posture as the sibling status components do.
findings.failureMode: A proactive work-pool automation fires on the absence of the chosen status event rather than when the pool stays in that status for the configured window.
findings.title: Work pool proactive status is stored in expect instead of after

String.split always returns at least one element, verified with node: "".split("
") is [""] and "a
".split("
") is ["a", ""], so the lines.length > 0 check can never select undefined and blank or trailing lines are stored as empty event names. Restore "strict": true.
findings.failureMode: Type validation and the production build accept strict-mode type errors across ui-v2 that the base configuration rejected, allowing latent runtime faults to merge undetected.
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode is disabled

findings.description: This is the only new threshold handler using global parseInt; every sibling (including this file's within handler) uses Number(e.target.value), and biome.json sets style useNumberNamespace to error with biome ci run in .github/workflows/ui-v2-checks.yml. Node verification also shows parseInt("") yields NaN and parseInt("2.9") truncates to 2, unlike Number. Use Number(e.target.value) to match the siblings and pass the lint rule.
findings.failureMode: Biome CI lint rejects the global parseInt, and clearing or entering a decimal threshold stores NaN or a silently truncated value.
findings.title: Work pool threshold uses global parseInt instead of Number

The onChange handler splits the textarea value on newlines and only stores undefined when lines.length is 0, but String.split always returns at least one element (verified: "".split("
") is [""], and "a
".split("
") is ["a", ""]). Clearing the textarea or ending it with a trailing newline therefore stores trigger.expect containing "", which passes z.array(z.string()) in automation-schema.ts. Fix by filtering out blank lines (and storing undefined when none remain).

findings.description: Every sibling threshold handler in this diff uses Number(e.target.value), and all other parseInt call sites in ui-v2 use Number.parseInt(value, 10); this one uses the global parseInt with no radix. Fix by using Number(e.target.value) like the other trigger components.
findings.failureMode: The ui-v2 Biome CI check fails on this file, and clearing the threshold input stores NaN.
findings.title: Work pool threshold uses bare parseInt without radix

findings.description: The new GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn declares availability.days as string[], but the base type came from listHandler's Prisma query where Availability.days is Int[] (packages/prisma/schema.prisma), i.e. number[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper passes each schedule to getScheduleListItemData, whose Schedule type in packages/lib/schedules/transformers requires days: number[], so the copied type no longer satisfies that existing caller.
findings.failureMode: Type-checking the atoms package fails at the schedule-list transformer call, and typed consumers are told numeric weekdays are strings.

findings.description: The moved Slot type declares userIds as string[], while the deleted base definition in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/types.ts had number[] and producers assign numeric ids (slots util maps users to user.id; features schedules slots use number[]). Slot is exposed through booker/types and the onTimeslotsLoaded callback, so integrators now compile against the wrong element type for runtime slot data.
findings.failureMode: Consumers comparing slot userIds against numeric user ids get type errors or false comparisons at runtime.
findings.title: Slot.userIds changed from number[] to string[]

findings.description: The new SlotInfo declares fromUser.id as string, but the original GetAvailableSlotsResponse was IGetAvailableSlots using IFromUser from getUserAvailability.ts, where id is number and is produced as { id: user.id }. The adjacent toUser.id is correctly kept as number, confirming the fromUser copy drifted. useAvailableSlots is exported from the atoms index, so its public return type now misdescribes out-of-office slot payloads.
findings.failureMode: Out-of-office handling that compares fromUser.id to a numeric user id fails to match or fails to compile against IFromUser-based types.

findings.failureMode: Biome lint fails on the two remaining QueryCell imports, blocking lint-staged commits touching them and leaving the atoms package in a permanently violating state.
findings.title: Widened Biome trpc ban breaks existing QueryCell imports

findings.description: The Slot type copied from trpc slots/types declares userIds?: string[], but the base type is userIds?: number[] and slot producers in trpc slots/util and features/schedules/lib/slots populate it from numeric user.id values. The public onTimeslotsLoaded callback therefore tells consumers the host IDs are strings while runtime values are numbers. Fix the line to userIds?: number[].
findings.failureMode: Consumers comparing slot userIds against string IDs per the type never match the numeric runtime IDs, selecting no or wrong hosts, and correct numeric code now fails to compile.
findings.title: Slot userIds typed as string[] instead of number[]

findings.description: SlotInfo.fromUser.id is declared string, but the source IFromUser in getUserAvailability has id: number, matching the toUser.id: number declared immediately below it in this same type. The copied GetAvailableSlotsResponse therefore mis-describes every out-of-office slot returned by _getAvailableSlots. Fix the line to id: number.
findings.failureMode: Out-of-office handling that compares fromUser.id as a string never matches the numeric runtime ID, so the away user is misidentified.
findings.title: SlotInfo fromUser id typed as string instead of number

findings.description: validateCreateScheduleInput only checks that input is an object with a non-empty name, then returns the whole object cast as CreateScheduleInput without validating schedule or eventTypeId. For example {name: 'x', schedule: 'bad', eventTypeId: 'abc'} passes validation, and the value later reaches getAvailabilityFromSchedule, which calls schedule.reduce and times.filter, or a Prisma connect with a non-numeric ID. Validate the nested schedule arrays of {start, end} Dates and numeric eventTypeId (as ZCreateInputSchema does) before returning.
findings.failureMode: Malformed schedule input passes validation and crashes schedule creation with a TypeError/500 instead of a validation error.
findings.title: validateCreateScheduleInput casts unchecked schedule and eventTypeId

findings.description: Both validation failures throw plain Error objects, violating the repository rule that custom errors extend a base type with a typed code (packages/lib/errors ErrorWithCode with ErrorCode, or HttpError with a status code). ErrorWithCode exists with codes such as ErrorCode.BadRequest for exactly this case. Throw a typed ErrorWithCode instead of new Error on this line and line 46.
findings.failureMode: Validation failures carry no code or status, so callers cannot branch on them and they surface as uncategorized 500-style errors rather than bad-request errors.
findings.title: Validator throws generic Error instead of typed error

findings.description: The new function uses single-quoted strings (this line and lines 40, 45, 46), while biome.json sets javascript formatter quoteStyle to double for the whole repository. The file is therefore not stable under the repo formatter and deviates from the mandated formatting configuration. Convert these literals to double quotes.
findings.failureMode: Running the repo Biome formatter rewrites this file, producing unexpected diff churn and formatter-check failures.
findings.title: Validator uses single quotes against Biome double-quote style

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction (for GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode, dispatched on a reader-mode tap in ToolbarMiddleware) was changed from displayView: .readerMode to .readerModeLongPressAction, duplicating handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction at line 590. In BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions, .readerMode calls toggleReaderMode() while .readerModeLongPressAction calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which adds the page to the reading list. Fix by restoring displayView: .readerMode.
findings.failureMode: Tapping the reader-mode button no longer toggles reader mode and instead adds the current page to the reading list.
findings.title: ShowReaderMode now triggers reading-list long-press action

findings.description: The filter changed from (isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL) to (isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL); since a reader-mode URL is http://localhost/reader-mode/page it already satisfies isWebPage(), so the exclusion is dropped (verified in URLExtension.swift). AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction uses toolbarAction.url ?? state.url, and urlDidChange normally stores tab.url.displayURL (the decoded original URL), so passing the raw reader URL overwrites it. Fix by restoring && !isReaderModeURL.
findings.failureMode: Cancelling edit in active Reader Mode replaces the address-bar URL with the internal localhost reader-mode URL instead of the original site URL.
findings.title: cancelEditMode no longer excludes reader-mode localhost URLs

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry changed .available from true to false and default from false to true (verified against the base revision), contradicting its own comment 'will be enabled after action gets executed' on the .available case. The unchanged ToolbarMiddlewareTests reader-mode test expects both recorded extras to be false for the default state, which the new default: true violates through readerModeButtonTapped. Fix by restoring .available: true and default: false.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode tap telemetry reports the opposite enabled state, corrupting reader-mode usage data and failing the existing reader-mode middleware test.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry enabled flag is inverted

findings.description: The changed line drops private from the gleanWrapper property, violating AGENTS.md Rule 11 requiring private for implementation details. Grep shows no caller outside ToolbarTelemetry reads this property (callers only pass it to init(gleanWrapper:)), so the wider internal access is unneeded and unrelated to the QR cleanup. Fix by restoring private let gleanWrapper.
findings.failureMode: Any code in the Client module can now access ToolbarTelemetry's internal Glean wrapper, breaking the encapsulation required by the repository access-control mandate.
findings.title: ToolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper access widened from private to internal
